doc.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021

title: Who keeps time in the trio
summary: Israels says everybody keeps time, since every tub sits on its own bottom.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Great point. At that time, much of this material that happened at the time — that’s not the right word, I’m struggling here. But the idea of, who is the timekeeper?
Everybody. And has it changed since the 50s and 60s to now, to current trios and quartets that are currently creating music now. Do you believe it has changed?

In principle I don’t think so. In practice it depends on who’s playing. The best principle is every tub sits on its own bottom. You know that? You know that? Every tub? That’s what that expression means. Everybody is responsible for his or her own timekeeping properties. You don’t want to be leaning heavily — every once in a while you get pushed off your foundation for a moment. And you’ve got to refer to somebody else for a split second. But it should only do that.
